alignments.note: Impersonal verb with the auxiliary and the indefinite subject pronoun *any* realizing its person and number (rule 17); head on the lexical verb.
Temporal `בְּ` recast as a finite clause takes the *when* (rule 52).
Suffix takes the subject pronoun the recasting writes for it (rules 18, 52).

`עַיִן` recast as the predicate *is on the watch*: the copula is the construction's (rule 20) and the supplied *on the* belongs to the nominal expression (rules 33, 15). Head on the word carrying the recast lexeme.
The second clause is asyndetic in the Hebrew; the coordinating *Or* answers to no morpheme (rule 14's closing sentence).
Verb with phrasal particle, headed on the verb (rule 44).
No suffix or other possessive morpheme stands on `אָף`; the supplied *his* is added (rule 18's closing sentence).
Indefinite article belongs to the noun (rule 15).

review_notes: *when he is on the watch* divides the temporal `בְּ` (*when*), its suffix (*he*) and the noun's recast predicate (*is on the watch*) under rules 52, 18 and 33.
*Or* and *his* are added: the Hebrew writes no conjunction in the second clause and no suffix on `אָף`.
